analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES Hot CPI and credit concerns; TSMC solid; VAT beats; Ericsson beats; Havas beats; Eutelsat up
key_insights: Global equities sold off sharply after hotter-than-expected US core inflation revived rate-hike concerns and deepened the unwind in AI trades. The Nasdaq fell 2%, the SOX 4.5% and software 3%, with neoclouds, servers and optical names hit hardest.

The selloff spread to Asia, where the Kospi fell 8% and Samsung and SK Hynix dropped more than 9%. High-beta, growth, momentum and liquidity factors underperformed. Defensive areas such as telcos and selected application software held up better.

The main concern was credit and AI financing. CoreWeave unsecured bonds traded into distressed territory (below 80 cents, yields above 15%), which highlighted leverage risk across AI neoclouds. The spillover hit Nebius and Oracle equity and credit.
Gartner published a view that much of the sector's planned AI investment may struggle to earn an adequate return. Some are also pointing to the latest Ramp AI Index showing slower employee AI spend.

GS Prime data after the NY close shows Global Fundamental LS managers down 0.8% (-1.7 StdDev), mainly beta, and down 2% MTD but up 10.6% YTD. TMT-focused funds fell 2.7% on the day (-2.6 StdDev) and are down 4.5% MTD but up 13% YTD.

TSMC Q3 was a modest beat. Revenue was a small beat, gross margin was broadly in line at 66.4%, operating margin was 58.7% vs 58.1% expected, and EPS was 4% ahead. Q4 revenue guidance of $52.3-54.3bn is above the Street's $50.35bn, and 2026 capex was held at $60-64bn.
GS says TSMC should reassure that AI deployment remains on track, but bulls had hoped for a further capex increase.

VAT Group reported organic orders up 188% (40% ahead of consensus) and a record book-to-bill of 1.9x. Management says there were no double bookings or inflated orders, even though lead times are now 9 months or more vs 3 months at the end of 2025. Chinese demand remains strong.

VAT guided 4Q sales to 420-450m (consensus 446m). 2027 guidance is expected significantly above 1.7bn (consensus 1.9bn, GSe 2.1bn). GS expects consensus to rise by a low double-digit percentage. The open question was whether the 2027 guide upgrade would come now or at Q4. The market reaction is likely held back by the global semis risk-off.

Ericsson beat on Q3 revenue (7% ahead at SEK59.48bn), gross margin (8% ahead) and cost control, with EBITA 28% ahead. GS notes it was a consensus short and expects a relative outperformance in this tape (up 3% on Tradegate on low volumes).

Ericsson's 4Q26 Networks revenue is guided in line with the 3-year average seasonality of +17% qoq, against consensus of +24% qoq off a lower base. Networks gross margin is guided to 49-51% vs consensus 48.3%. GS expects FY street topline estimates up about 3% with better drop-through. The RAN market is guided flat, geopolitical uncertainty is elevated and component costs are a gross margin headwind next year.

Havas Q3 organic growth of 2.4% was slightly ahead of expectations, with stronger momentum in Europe and North America. Revenue rose 7.2% to €703m, helped by FX and acquisitions. Guidance of 2-3% organic growth and a 13.2-13.5% margin was reiterated and the expected M&A contribution was raised to 2.5%. The GS analyst raised FY26-27 EBIT forecasts by 2-3%.

ASML closed up despite most of semicap ending down. Capacity expansion dominated the Q&A, with a targeted 30% increase in 2027 and further growth in 2028. Management avoided precise unit guidance given lead times of more than 12 months. At least two potential new EUV customers were indicated for 2029-30, including Terafab.

ASML gross margin should benefit from higher volumes, fixed-cost absorption, a stronger EUV and immersion mix, upgrade revenue and price increases. GS expects street estimates to rise over the next few days on the gross margin surprise.

Reports say China has a domestic EUV light source prototype that could be ready for mass production in 3-5 years. GS sees no near-term commercial threat. The prototype outputs 15W, against ASML's 250W sources deployed since 2018 and a move toward 1,000W.

Eutelsat rose 23% on reports of Starlink restrictions in Ukraine, reflecting its position as Europe's only meaningful low-Earth-orbit satellite alternative. It is unclear how long the restrictions last, and Starlink access was restored after a similar earlier episode.

US trading: the first -1% SPX and -2% NDX move since late July, with neoclouds down 12% (a top-5 move in 5 years). Core CPI was 33bps vs 20bps consensus on firmer shelter. Market pricing for a Fed hike is 35% for October and 87% for December, and GIR expects a second hike in December.

GS desk flow: asset managers and hedge funds were net sellers on overlapping tech and macro supply, and the info tech sell skew hit its highest in more than 4 weeks. Major index ETF volumes ran +40-60%, which suggests heavy top-down selling.

Accenture gave 3-year targets of mid-single-digit local-currency revenue growth for FY27 and FY28, accelerating to mid-to-high single digits in FY29, with operating margin expanding 10-30bps per year. Capgemini is guided to 5.5-7.5% constant-currency growth (200bps from M&A, so 3.5-5.5% organic) and 40-50bps of annual margin expansion. Publicis comments on Sapient were also supportive.

Workday Analyst Day: GIR sees a stronger long-term AI position, with Sana as a unified front end, faster internal agent development, headless deployment options and a proposed C1.ai acquisition. Management estimates an incremental $100bn TAM. GIR stays Neutral because integration challenges, data readiness and internal resistance are slowing deployment, so agentic AI adoption likely follows an S-curve.

RELX (Buy): GS argues the market prices an overly severe AI bear case for Legal, which is only 12% of group EBIT, with the shares at 17x 2027E EPS. Proprietary legal datasets and more token-efficient AI tools should let RELX hold subscription pricing and support about 10% Legal revenue growth. The shares have a strong negative correlation with the GS AI EU leaders basket.

At OCP Global Summit 2026, NVIDIA unveiled an NVLink switch board using PTFE materials for the Vera Rubin AI server architecture and named 7 supply chain partners, including Taiflex, Flexium, TTM, Shengyi, Shennan, Victory Giant and Kinwong.
Industry expects Google suppliers led by TSMC, Mediatek and Hon Hai to see growth from the release of Google's Gemini 4 Argon.

UMG is cutting jobs across US, UK, German and Canadian operations as part of a cost programme begun in February 2024 that ends next year. Stagwell announced a three-year collaboration with ServiceNow. Revolut started a German mobile service on the Telefonica network. Liberty Global named Rocío Lorenzo CEO of Telenet from November 2, 2026. Rightmove reported Q3 asking rents up 2.4%.

Ericsson Q3 (reported 10/15): revenue SEK59.48bn, 7% ahead of expectations. EBITA 10.12bn vs 7.93bn expected, a 28% beat, with margin 17% vs street 14.3%. 4Q26 Networks revenue guided to roughly +17% qoq vs consensus +24% qoq off a lower base. Networks gross margin guided to 49-51% vs consensus 48.3%.

Havas Q3 (reported 10/15): organic growth 2.4%, slightly ahead of expectations. Revenue +7.2% to €703m including FX and acquisitions. FY guidance of 2-3% organic growth and 13.2-13.5% margin reiterated, M&A contribution raised to 2.5%. The GS analyst raised FY26-27 EBIT forecasts by 2-3%.
ASML (call 10/14): management targets a 30% capacity increase in 2027 and further growth in 2028, and street gross margin estimates are expected to rise after a gross margin surprise.

Accenture (company targets, not reported results): mid-single-digit local-currency revenue growth for FY27 and FY28, operating margin expansion of 10-30bps per year for FY27 to FY29. Capgemini guidance of 5.5-7.5% constant-currency growth including 200bps from M&A and 40-50bps of annual margin expansion over 3 years.
Publicis commented on Sapient that the US was positive in Q3, and guided Q4 to turn positive globally.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Printed this morning, hotter than expected on firmer shelter categories. It revived rate-hike concerns and triggered the risk-off.
Consensus expectation that the print exceeded.
Front-end pricing was significantly compressed from its highs before the print, so the market rebuilt near-term hike risk.
GIR continues to expect it and looks to tomorrow's PPI report and Warsh's speech in Bangkok for soundbites.

macro_indicators.indicator: Rightmove UK asking rents, annual increase
macro_indicators.interpretation: Available London rental homes are down 9% on the year and renter demand is up 6%. Elevated mortgage rates make property investment less attractive to prospective landlords.

risk_factors: Credit and financing stress in AI neoclouds and hyperscaler bonds, including CoreWeave unsecured bonds at distressed levels.
Gartner's view that planned AI investment may not earn an adequate return, plus a slowdown in employee AI spend per the Ramp AI Index.
Hotter inflation raising Fed hike odds, with PPI and Warsh's Bangkok speech as near-term catalysts.
Additional AI concerns listed by GS: OpenAI revenue confusion, Chinese memory breakthroughs easing bottlenecks, datacenter sentiment into midterms, power and shell constraints, and further issuance.
Ericsson flagged elevated geopolitical uncertainty and component cost headwinds to gross margin next year.
Possible ASML capacity limits on semiconductor equipment market growth, which GS is not convinced by.
Workday AI adoption risk from integration challenges, data readiness and internal resistance.
